findings.title: dora_keys.cfr_keyings exclusion is inert: `record` never equals the check-run name `governance / record`
findings.claim: dora_keys.cfr_keyings drops an exclusion key only when it equals the full check-run name (`names - drop`). Since the layout cut-over every governance job reports as `<unit> / <job>`, so cfr_exclusions.json's only key `record` matches nothing: over the window's 271 merges cfr_merge_keyed equals cfr_merge_unexcluded (0.808, delta 0.0), while keying the same list on the job id drops the 3 merges whose only red is `governance / record` (0.797, delta 0.011). The brief's own control -- one job added to the exclusion list moves the rate by exactly that job's count -- fails on the instrument: --exclude record leaves the instrument's rate at 0.808.

evidence.unit: cfr_raw_excl_delta_merge (rate delta the exclusion buys in dora_keys.cfr_keyings); job-keyed delta 0.011 (3 merges)
evidence.machine: box B8 (light seat), Linux 6.18.44 container; network-bound, GitHub-reported durations and counts
evidence.contention_note: shared box during fan-out; the number is a count / GitHub-reported duration, contention-immune

findings.title: instrument-self-tests red on main at 200 of 271 merges, green at 186 of their heads; time to restore 106 h, still open
findings.claim: Per check-run name, `governance / instrument-self-tests` concluded failure at 200 of the window's 271 merge commits (0.738) and at 18 of their 271 pull-request heads; at 186 merges it failed at the merge commit after passing at the head. Its red episodes on main: 2, median 65.82 h, max 106.19 h, one still open at the window's end, against the required `gate`'s 19 episodes of median 0.34 h. It is the only failing name at 162 merges, so it alone carries the merge-keyed change-failure rate from 0.24 to 0.808. The logs read at four failures show the drift check (`tools/ci/selftest_scope.py check`, which its docstring runs only on a push to main) refusing 11 then 27 steps: a red that no pull-request head can see, which then stands on main for days and masks any new red of the job.

findings.phenomenon_property: A job whose check runs on a push to main also runs, with the same verdict, at the pull-request head that produced the merge, so its red is answered before the merge rather than restored after it

findings.title: governance_cost.py reads 10.7% of the CI seconds a merge pays: final head only, latest attempt only
findings.claim: governance_cost.py sums check-run durations at a pull request's FINAL head from the default check-runs listing, which returns the latest attempt only. Over the window's 271 merges that surface reads 3,100,885 s of the 28,895,795 s their CI ran at every commit of the pull request (filter=all) plus the merge commit: omitted_share 0.893 (by day 0.857..0.921 over 8 day-cells; 0.896 with the lowest day dropped; 0.887 with runs deduplicated across stacked PRs). Mean seconds per merge read 11,442 against 106,627 paid, a 9.3x under-read. At the final heads alone the default listing hides 37,189 run attempts (5,331,965 s) that filter=all returns, although d11lib.check_runs's docstring says the listing shows a re-run. The governance share barely moves (0.204 vs 0.186), so the split survives; the per-merge cost the instrument reports does not.

evidence.unit: omitted_share = 1 - head-surface seconds / all seconds paid
